title.narrative: Output 3.4. Increased capacity of ILO constituents to promote peaceful, stable and resilient societies through decent work

description.narrative:
Targeted municipalities in seven Governorates have improved capacities to manage employment intensive projects and improved awareness of municipality and Ministry of Labour officers on labour laws, work permits, and social security rules and regulations. As a result, Syrian refugees have enhanced access to formal labour market and decent work through eased work permit scheme. The Government of Jordan has also adopted national safety guidelines for COVID-19 for the Cash for Work sector which are being used as guidance throughout the sector. These safety guidelines will add to the Cash for Work sector SOPs, the development of which continued as more agencies and projects joined KfW and GIZ, hastening the need for sector consistency.
The Ministry of Local Administration (MOLA) increased the labour intensity of the Municipality Services and Social Resilience Projects (MSSRP), thereby achieving 27,438 Worker-days during the municipal grants cycle one. In addition, the MOLA improved the decent working conditions of workers in the contracts documents for the construction sector by applying the Fédération Internationale des Ingénieurs - Conseils (FIDIC) standards and supplementary particular conditions. The MOLA, with ILO and World Bank support, developed the recruitment strategy for the MSSRP to promote transparency in hiring the workers.
In addition, 30 engineers and technicians from the MOLA and municipalities in Irbid and Mafraq governorates have improved their knowledge and capacity in implementing labour intensive methods in public works projects. This generated 15,000 workdays in labour based projects in 3 municipalities in Irbid and Mafraq governorates.
The Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, with ILO and UNESCO support, has implemented a labour-intensive approach to rehabilitate three cultural heritage sites in Jordan, thereby creating 518 jobs and generating up to 53,872 workerdays, while adhering to decent working principles. The ILO, as the co-lead of the Cash for Work (CFW) Working Group in Jordan, established in April 2021 a Program Support Unit within the Ministry of Labour (MOL) whose function is to coordinate and support the MOL in the issuance of work permits for Syrian refugees. With the support of the German Government, the ILO has entered into a partnership with the General Federation of Jordanian Trade Unions in order to issue flexible work permits to 675 Syrians in 2021, which allows them the flexibility to work for any employer in the construction sector for a period of a year. In addition, the ILO, as co-lead of the CFW Working Group, led the drafting of the COVID-19 safety guidelines for the sector and supported the adoption by the government.
With support from the World Bank, the ILO provided technical support to the Ministry of Local Administration (MOLA) by conducting trainings on implementing and monitoring EIIP, implementing Labour Resources-Based projects and conducting tenders.
With support of the Italian government, and in partnership with the JEA, the ILO conducted trainings for the municipalities' staff on labour intensive methods in public works projects. The ILO provided technical guidance and on-site coaching for the field staff of 3 municipalities in Irbid and Mafraq governorates.
With support from the EU, the ILO worked closely with UNESCO and its technical archaeological partner to finalise the work plan for two heritage sites. The ILO developed the employment intensive approach particular conditions that were included in the contract documents. Jointly with UNESCO, the ILO also conducted costing training for the prospective bidders and participated in the technical committee for evaluating the offers. Finally, the ILO conducted pre-commencement training for the local subcontracted NGO (Bithourna for Technical Training and Capacity Building - BTCB) personnel on the employment intensive approach.

Output 3.3. Increased capacity of member States to formulate and implement policies for a just transition towards environmentally sustainable economies and societies

description.narrative: The national government and 11 local municipalities from Irbid, Mafraq, Jerash, Ajloun, Amman, Karak and Zarqa Governorates have implemented environmental sustainability measures through the Employment-Intensive Infrastructure Programme (EIIP), resulting in cleaner public spaces and greater community awareness. With support from the German government through KfW, the ILO through the Employment-Intensive Infrastructure Programme (EIIP) project has supported the national government and the local municipalities in environmental cleaning in public areas and safe waste disposal by providing short-term employment to over 4,000 Syrian refugees and Jordanians hired to support this work. Moreover, the ILO conducted an environmental awareness campaign for the wider youth community during early 2021. The virtual campaign reached more than 100,000 people through social media.
